input: Learn to tie five essential sailing knots

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: There are many sailing knots to choose from — knowing which five the user wants to learn (or whether they need help choosing) determines the entire content of the plan.
Whether this is for a solo adult learner, a child, or a group (e.g. a sailing class) changes the teaching approach, pace, and materials needed.
Whether they are learning for active on-water sailing, a shore-based course, or general interest affects which knots are prioritised and how practice should be structured.
Knowing their current skill level with knots or sailing avoids explaining things they already know and sets the right starting point.
Knowing what materials they have available (rope, a cleat, a railing, instructional books/videos) determines what practice methods are feasible right now.
People learn knots differently — some prefer step-by-step diagrams, others prefer video demonstrations or hands-on repetition drills — shaping how the plan is structured.
Knowing the target standard — tying from memory, tying quickly under pressure, or just recognising and tying slowly — sets a clear definition of 'done' for each knot.

gold.taskTitle: Learn to tie five essential sailing knots
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to learn how to tie five essential sailing knots, likely for practical use on the water or as a foundational sailing skill.

questions.title: Which five specific knots do you want to learn?
questions.description: Identify whether the user already has five knots in mind (e.g. bowline, cleat hitch, clove hitch, reef knot, figure-eight) or needs recommendations.

questions.title: Who is learning — you alone, or a group?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a solo adult learner, a child, or multiple people such as a sailing crew or class.

questions.title: Is this for active sailing, a course, or general interest?
questions.description: Establish the real-world context — on-water use, a formal sailing qualification, or casual personal interest — to prioritise the right knots and practice scenarios.

questions.title: How much knot-tying experience do you already have?
questions.description: Gauge the user's current baseline so the plan starts at the right level — complete beginner, familiar with a few knots, or experienced with ropework generally.

questions.title: What materials do you have available to practise with?
questions.description: Find out whether the user has rope, a cleat, a rail, or other props on hand, and whether they have access to books, apps, or instructional videos.

questions.title: Do you learn best from diagrams, video, or hands-on drills?
questions.description: Identify the user's preferred learning style to shape whether the plan emphasises written step-by-step instructions, video resources, or timed repetition practice.

questions.title: What does success look like — slow and accurate, or fast from memory?
questions.description: Clarify the target standard: tying each knot once correctly with guidance, tying reliably from memory, or tying quickly under real sailing conditions.
